text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of fractures, severe acne, and delayed menarche, I need to clarify the cause of your birth defects and current hormonal status. Did you have a chromosomal karyotype analysis performed recently? REQUEST TEST: Karyotype

speaker: Doctor
text: The karyotype results are normal, which helps rule out complete androgen insensitivity syndrome given your history of partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly. Given your history of fractures from minor trauma and severe acne, do you have a known family history of early osteoporosis or brittle bones? REQUEST TEST: Bone_Density_Scan (DEXA)

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal karyotype and DEXA scan help narrow the differential, but your history of birth defects like partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly, combined with severe acne and bone fragility, is highly specific. Do you have a family history of short stature or hypertrichosis (excessive hair growth)? REQUEST TEST: 17-Hydroxyprogesterone

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency).
